text: your heart is a muscle that pumps blood
to all parts of your body when you have
heart failure your heart has trouble
keeping up with the amount of blood that
it needs to pump for normal function
heart failure is called congestive
because as the heart has more trouble
pumping blood it can cause fluid to back
up in the body heart failure is a
chronic condition there is no cure for
heart failure and we want your heart to
work as well as it can every day you
need to make good choices to protect
your heart we want you to have a good
quality of life
besides taking your medications and
going to the cardiac rehabilitation how
you eat is very important in helping
your heart work as well as it can
here are three main nutrition things
that you can do for a healthy heart when
you have heart failure
the first is to follow a low-salt or low
sodium diet that is no more than 2,000
milligrams of sodium this will help your
heart work much better please view our
low sodium diet video for details on how
to follow a low sodium diet this is an
important part of the diet for heart
failure secondly drink no more than 64
ounces of total fluids a day you want to
limit your fluids to no more than 64
ounces a day or 2,000 milliliters which
is the amount of a two-liter bottle a
pop we don't want you to drink pop
because it's not good for your body but
the amount and a two-liter bottle is a
good picture to have in mind when
managing your fluid intake it's
important to balance your fluids and
salt for a healthy heart diet keep in
mind if you eat less salt you will be
less thirsty limiting fluids includes
common fluids like water juice milk
coffee and tea as well as foods that are
liquid at room temperature like ice
cream popsicles and jello soups can also
be a major source of fluid they are high
in sodium usually so it might be best to
avoid these altogether let's go over
ways to track your fluids choose the
method
works best for you use your hospital
water pitcher if you have half a liter
pitcher it can be refilled three times
per day for 1500 milliliters this leaves
up to 500 milliliters more for fluid and
foods such as ice cream adding ice to
drinks taking medications or drinking
water when brushing your teeth the lines
on the pitcher will show you how many
milliliters or ounces you have drink
note if you have a large hospital water
pitcher at home use a limit of one and a
half refills or in the morning pour 64
ounces or 2,000 milliliters of water
into a large pitcher or a two liter soda
bottle every time you drink any kind of
fluid pour out that same amount of water
from the pitcher when the pitcher is
empty you will have reached your fluid
limit for the day you can also pour
drinks into 8 8 ounce cups for a total
of 64 ounces or 2,000 milliliters use
smaller cups and increase the number of
portions for more beverage variety
please refer to the limiting your fluids
handout in your heart failure book for
more tips on how to do this the last
thing we want to cover is weighing
yourself each and every day please be
sure to weigh yourself after using the
bathroom and before breakfast every
morning weigh yourself at about the same
time wearing clothing of similar weights
or no clothes at all to get an accurate
measure of weights be sure to call the
heart failure nurse navigator or your
cardiologists if you gain two pounds or
more in a single day or if you gain 5
pounds or more in a week by following
these recommendations you can actively
manage your condition and help have a
better quality of life with heart
failure for more information including
limiting fluids low sodium diet menus
foodless for a low sodium diet and how
to season food without salt please check
our patient education handouts on this
topic
